annotations.title: Court-reported negative history for one case

description: Later courts, in their own words, reporting that one case was overruled, abrogated, superseded, reversed or vacated. Takes a cluster id (the case-record id), not an opinion id. Every row carries the citing court’s own sentence, cut from its stored text; the label is a filter over those sentences, not a verdict, and 68.7% of findings are expressly partial ("overruled on other grounds"). Not a validity verdict and not Shepardizing: an automated, unverified reading with no positive signal, so zero rows is not evidence that a case remains good law. Rows include known false positives; a read guard (version 2) withholds ten known false shapes and counts them in declined_by_read_guard with read_guard_note. Precision, hand-read after version 2: 0.9862 (95% interval 0.9511-0.9962, 145 of 150 kept rows); 1.0000 (0.9124-1.0000, 40 of 40) for cases cited 10,000+ times. Recall for this collection is unknown; the only figure, 0.6477 (0.5780-0.7116, n=193), is an upper bound on the Supreme Court stratum. The overruling opinion itself is usually not among the rows (Roe carries no row from Dobbs). Five labels only; "followed" and "distinguished" are not loaded. Counts are for this record alone; also_carried_by names sibling records. unrelayable_in_window counts rows dropped because no sentence could be cut; capped=true marks a slice; order is citing-opinion date. Case law in this mirror ends 2026-09-30 (exact scan of all 10,174,547 case records): a thin or empty result for recent authority means the collection ends there, not that no such case exists. Every response carries a "note" and a coverage_note. The sources tool returns this tool’s full coverage statement.

cluster_id.description: the CASE RECORD (cluster) id of the case you are checking — from a search/citation/fts result (id or cluster_id), not an opinion id

label.description: filter rows to one label. A filter over sentences, never a verdict; by_label on the response reports all five regardless

offset.description: skip this many, for paging further down the date order; capped at 5000
